memory_annotations.evidence_summary: Maya selected the Southwest daytime nonstop itinerary for this San Diego trip after comparing all-in baggage costs, schedules, and usable vacation time. This was a trip-specific decision, not a recurring preference.

messages.content: I have the three San Diego flight options now. Can you compare them for both of us with one shared checked bag and tell me which one makes the most sense for the five-night trip?
Yes. Send me the fare, schedule, stops, and bag charge for each option. I’ll compare the true round-trip cost and how much time each leaves you in San Diego.

Option one is $718 total before bags. It leaves MSP at 6:10 a.m. Sunday and lands in San Diego at 8:03 a.m. nonstop. The Friday return leaves at 8:45 p.m. and gets to Minneapolis at 2:08 a.m. Saturday. One checked bag is $60 each way.

That option is $838 for two travelers after the $120 round-trip bag charge. It provides nearly the full arrival and departure days, but it requires a very early start Sunday and an overnight arrival home after the trip.
Option two is Southwest at $874 total. Both flights are nonstop. Sunday is 9:05 a.m. to 11:10 a.m., and Friday is 12:35 p.m. to 5:55 p.m. The checked bag is included.

Southwest stays at $874 all-in for the two of you. It costs $36 more than option one, reaches San Diego about three hours later, and gives up most of Friday afternoon, but both travel days are much easier and there is no separate bag payment to track.

The third is $766 before the bag. It connects in Denver going out and Salt Lake City coming back. It leaves at 10:30 a.m. Sunday and arrives at 3:50 p.m. The return is 1:30 p.m. to 8:40 p.m. The bag is $35 each way.

With one shared checked bag, option three totals $836. It is $38 below Southwest and $2 below option one, but the outbound connection costs most of your first afternoon. It also adds two connection points where a delay could affect the itinerary.
Can you put each one against the single-hotel plan? I want to see how close we are to the $3,600 ceiling.

Using the current five-night hotel total of $2,015: option one brings airfare and lodging to $2,853, leaving $747; Southwest totals $2,889, leaving $711; and option three totals $2,851, leaving $749. All three are comfortably under the $3,600 airfare-and-lodging ceiling.
So the connection saves only $38 compared with Southwest?

Correct. The connected itinerary is $836 with the shared checked bag, versus $874 on Southwest. The $38 savings comes with a 3:50 p.m. arrival instead of 11:10 a.m. and two connections across the round trip.
And the early nonstop only saves $36 once the bag is included.
Right. Its advertised fare is much lower, but after the bag fee it is $838. The remaining $36 savings requires a pre-dawn airport arrival on Sunday and getting home shortly after 2:00 a.m. Saturday.
Select Southwest. The extra $36 to $38 is worth the cleaner schedule, and $2,889 still leaves enough room. Don’t book it yet.

Southwest is selected for the working plan: two nonstop round trips, MSP-SAN November 8 and SAN-MSP November 13, for $874 total with the shared checked bag included. Paired with the current $2,015 single-hotel estimate, the airfare-and-lodging total is $2,889, leaving $711 under the $3,600 ceiling. The other two flight options are declined. Nothing has been booked; the fare, bag inclusion, hotel total, fees, and cancellation terms still need confirmation before purchase.
